extracted.intended_audience: applicants filing PCT international applications and their representatives (patent attorneys); receiving Offices and International Searching Authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing and correcting PCT international applications in the international phase, covering required content (title, abstract, language, physical form), correction procedures and time limits, priority claims and declarations, record/search copy transmission, and the international search procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of a title
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must contain a title (that is, a title for the claimed invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of a title is a defect under Article 14(1)(a)(iv), Rule 8 and may give rise to an invitation to correct. Corrections generally must be made within applicable time limits (see correction rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of an abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must contain an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of an abstract is a defect (Article 14(1)(a)(iv), Rule 8) that the receiving Office may invite the applicant to correct within the prescribed time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with prescribed physical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must comply with the prescribed physical requirements (specified in Rule 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance must be checked only to the extent necessary for reasonably uniform international publication. An international application will not be considered withdrawn for lack of full compliance if it complies to the extent necessary for reasonably uniform international publication (Article 14(1)(a)(v), Rule 11, Rule 26.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for application elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any element of the international application, other than the description and claims, must be in an admitted language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If elements are not in an admitted language (Article 3(4)(i), Rule 12.1, Rule 26.3ter(a)), the receiving Office may invite correction. Some Offices have incompatibilities with Rule 26.3ter(a); where incompatible, all elements must comply with Rule 12.1 before an international filing date can be accorded (see Annex C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to correct defects and two‑month time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office invites the applicant to correct defects; the time limit for filing the correction is two months from the date of the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the correction is made within the time limit (including any extension), the international filing date remains the date on which the application was received; otherwise the application is considered withdrawn (Article 14(1)(b), Rule 26.1, Rule 26.2, Rule 26.2bis(b), Rule 26.3ter(b), Rule 26.5, Rule 29.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when filed in a language not accepted by the receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is filed in a language not accepted by the national/regional Office but accepted by the International Bureau as receiving Office, the national/regional Office will date‑stamp and promptly transmit it to the International Bureau which acts as receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal may be subject to a transmittal fee; other fees paid to the national/regional Office will be refunded and applicable fees paid to the International Bureau. The international application so transmitted is considered received by the International Bureau on the date it was received by the national/regional Office for most purposes, but time limits for paying fees due on filing are computed from the date actually received by the International Bureau (Rule 19.4(a)(ii), Rule 19.4(b), Rule 19.4(c); Annex C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing with a non‑competent receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files with a national/regional Office that acts as a receiving Office but is not competent for the applicant's residence/nationality, the application is considered received by that Office on behalf of the International Bureau as receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will date‑stamp and transmit the application to the International Bureau; transmittal may be subject to a fee equal to the transmittal fee; applicable fees will then have to be paid to the International Bureau (Rule 19.4(a)(i), Rule 19.4(b), Rule 19.4(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of indications of residence and nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: If indications of applicant’s residence and nationality as stated in the request do not support the right to file with that receiving Office, the receiving Office issues an invitation to correct under Article 11(1)(i) and Rule 4.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may submit evidence and a proposed correction; if the receiving Office is satisfied, the invitation will be considered to correct defects under Article 14(1)(a)(ii) and Rule 4.5 and indications may be corrected so as not to affect the international filing date. Note that some Offices (e.g., USPTO) may not apply this procedure (Article 11(1)(i), Article 14(1)(a)(ii), Rule 4.5, Section 329).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time limits for certain corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: The two‑month time limit for correction of defects under Article 14(1) may be extended by the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving Office may extend the time limit ex officio or at the applicant’s request at any time—even after expiry—before a decision on whether the correction was timely is taken (Rule 26.2). Time limits for correction under Article 11 or Article 14(2) and for payment of missing or underpaid fees under Rule 16bis may not be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and addition of priority claims (time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any defective priority claim may be corrected and any missing priority claim added by notice to the receiving Office or International Bureau within time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limit: 16 months from the priority date (or 16 months from a changed priority date, whichever 16‑month period expires first); in any event, notice may be submitted until the expiration of four months from the international filing date. A correction received before a declaration of void and not later than one month after expiration of the applicable time limit is considered timely. Obvious mistakes may be rectified under Rule 91 within 26 months from the priority date provided rectification does not change the earliest priority date (Rule 26bis.1(a), Rule 26bis.2(b), Rule 91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of early publication request on priority‑claim corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has requested early publication, any notice to correct or add a priority claim received after that request will be considered not to have been submitted unless the request is withdrawn before technical preparations for publication are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants requesting early publication should be aware they may lose the ability to correct/add priority claims unless they withdraw the early publication request in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalculation of time limits when priority date changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Where correction/addition of a priority claim causes a change in the priority date, any time limit computed from the previously applicable priority date that has not already expired will be computed from the priority date as changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should re‑calculate deadlines after any priority date change (Rule 26bis.1(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to correct priority claims (grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office or International Bureau may invite correction of a priority claim where: (i) the international filing date is later than the priority period and no restoration request submitted; (ii) the priority claim does not comply with Rule 4.10; or (iii) any indication in the priority claim is not the same as the corresponding indication in the priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such invitations are issued under Rule 26bis.2; applicants should respond within applicable time limits to avoid a declaration that the claim is void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing applicant of restoration possibility when filing date outside priority period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the filing date is outside the 12‑month priority period but within two months after it expired, the receiving Office informs the applicant of the possibility to request restoration of the right of priority (subject to national law incompatibilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies except where Rule 26bis.3 is incompatible with the national law applied by that Office (Rule 26bis.2(a), Rule 26bis.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to answer invitation to correct priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant fails to respond to an invitation to correct a priority claim before the expiration of the time limit, that priority claim will be considered void for the purposes of the PCT procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: a priority claim will not be considered void only because the earlier application number is missing, an indication in the claim differs from the priority document, or the international filing date is later than the priority date provided the international filing date is within two months of that date (Rule 26bis.2(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of information when priority claim declared void or possibly defective
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office or International Bureau declares a priority claim void (or it is not considered void only due to Rule 26bis.2(c)), the International Bureau will publish information concerning the priority claim together with any information submitted by the applicant prior to completion of technical preparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant wishes to correct/add a priority claim after Rule 26bis.1 time limit has expired, they may request IB to publish information on the matter prior to expiration of 30 months from the priority date and pay a special fee (Section 113(c) Administrative Instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction/addition of declarations under Rule 4.17 (time limits and form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any defective declaration may be corrected and any new declaration added by notice to the International Bureau; time limit is 16 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections received after the time limit are considered received on the last day of the time limit if they reach the IB before technical preparations for publication are completed (Rule 26ter.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of defects in Rule 4.17 declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Defects that may give rise to an invitation to correct include lack of standardized wording, blank spaces not filled (names, dates), or, for U.S. inventorship declarations, missing prescribed signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office or IB may invite correction under Rule 26ter.2(a). Correct the standardized wording and fill blanks as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of corrected or added declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections/additions of declarations must be made by notice consisting of the corrected/added declaration itself accompanied by a letter explaining the correction/addition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notices should be submitted directly to the International Bureau in all cases, even if in response to an invitation by the receiving Office. Any notice submitted to the receiving Office will be date stamped and transmitted to the IB (Section 216, Section 317).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheet requirements for corrected declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a corrected declaration, the applicant must submit a replacement sheet using the relevant Box (Boxes Nos. VIII (i) to (v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For added declarations, applicant may use the relevant sub‑box or a blank sheet. Corrected/added U.S. inventorship declarations should be signed and dated by the inventor and entitled 'Supplemental declaration of inventorship (Rules 4.17(iv) and 51bis.1(a)(iv))' (Section 214(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of declarations even if non‑compliant or uncorrected
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau will publish declarations, either as originally filed or as corrected, whether or not they comply with Rule 4.17; an indication that declarations were made will be included on the front page of the published international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure declarations are correct and compliant because IB will publish them regardless (Rule 48.2(b)(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling corrections received after the time limit for declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: If IB receives a correction/addition of a declaration after the applicable time limit, it notifies the applicant, does not publish or communicate that declaration to designated Offices, and informs applicant that such declarations should be submitted directly to designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the case of a declaration of inventorship signed by at least one inventor, IB will return the declaration to the applicant (Rule 26ter.1, Section 419(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IB may note defects and require receiving Office to invite correction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IB finds defects (not signed by at least one applicant as provided, prescribed applicant name not present, missing prescribed indications for applicants, or non‑compliance with physical requirements), it brings such defects to the attention of the receiving Office, which must invite correction within two months unless it believes there is no defect (Rule 28).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an additional check beyond the receiving Office; applicants should ensure signatures, names and prescribed indications are present and physical requirements met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form for filing corrections generally (replacement sheets and explanatory letter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections must generally be filed as replacement sheet(s) incorporating the correction and accompanied by a letter explaining differences between the replacement sheet and the one it replaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction by letter without replacement sheets is possible only for corrections of the request where the correction can be transferred without adverse effect on clarity and reproducibility. Refer to Rule 92.1 for signature and other requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fee for requesting or making corrections; extensions free
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the request for and the making of any correction are free of charge; there is also no fee for extension of a time limit for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should take advantage of free corrections and free extensions (where permitted) to preserve rights (paragraph 6.053).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited remedies/appeals during the international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT does not expressly provide for appeals or petitions during the international phase, but practice shows receiving Offices may reconsider decisions on petition and some national courts/appeal boards have accepted appeals against decisions taken by national/regional Offices acting as receiving Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a successful appeal may be without effect in designated States if the applicant has not performed required acts under Articles 22(1), 39(1)(a), or 25 within applicable time limits (paragraph 6.054).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Office review of receiving Office decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT provides for review by designated Offices of any decision of the receiving Office refusing to accord an international filing date or declaring the application withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of the procedure, including time limits for requesting review, are handled in the National Phase (Article 25, Rule 29.1, Rule 51).

rubrics_metrics.name: National law discretion to excuse delays in meeting time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State must excuse delays in meeting time limits for reasons allowed by national law; a Contracting State may excuse delays for other reasons at its discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices may maintain the effect of an international application even where the receiving Office decision declaring withdrawal is found correct; consult national phase rules for details (Article 24(2), Article 48(2), Rule 82bis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record copy must reach the International Bureau in time
rubrics_metrics.description: The record copy (considered the true copy of the international application for PCT procedure) must reach the International Bureau within the prescribed time limit; otherwise the international application is considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, no application will be considered withdrawn without prior information to the applicant. Failure to transmit the record copy does not relieve applicant of obligation to enter national phase within applicable time limits (Article 12(2), Article 12(3), Article 22(1), Article 24(1)(ii), Article 24(1)(iii), Rule 22.1, Rule 22.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau monitoring and remediation for missing record copy
rubrics_metrics.description: IB monitors receipt of the record copy: if not received within 13 months from the priority date, IB urges the receiving Office; one month later IB notifies the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After notification, applicant can ask the receiving Office to transmit the record copy or to issue a certified copy free of charge which applicant can transmit to IB. After three months from the IB notification, IB may find that no record copy was received. Certification of a copy must be free except in certain cases (Rule 20.2(c), Rule 22.1(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search copy transmission conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The search copy is transmitted by the receiving Office to the International Searching Authority only if the international search fee has been fully paid and, where the application was filed in a language not accepted by the ISA, only after the required translation has been furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should pay the search fee and, where applicable, furnish translations promptly to avoid delays in establishing the international search report. The ISA notifies IB, applicant and RO of receipt of the search copy (Article 12(1), Rule 12.1(c), Rule 23.1, Rule 25.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of certified copies from the receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request and payment of a fee, the receiving Office must furnish certified copies of the international application as filed and of any corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certified copy of the international application is the priority document when claiming priority of that international application (Rule 21.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: International search main procedural steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The main procedural steps before the International Searching Authority are: (i) conducting the international search, (ii) preparing the international search report, and (iii) establishing a written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are fundamental stages of the international search procedure (Article 15, Article 18, Rule 43, Rule 43bis.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence and choice of International Searching Authority (ISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each receiving Office specifies one or more ISAs competent to carry out international searches on applications filed with it; where several are specified the applicant may choose between them subject to language restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex D and Annex C indicate competent ISAs and languages accepted. Where application filed with IB as RO, competent ISA(s) are those that would have been competent if filed with a competent national/regional Office. ISAs may provide limitations of competence under specific agreements (Article 16, Rule 4.14bis, Rule 35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant comments on earlier search results
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an international application claims priority to an earlier application that was searched by the same Office acting as ISA, some ISAs will consider applicant comments on earlier search results when carrying out the international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants wishing that comments be considered should submit them to the receiving Office with the international application (typically by checking Box No. IX, sub‑box 'Other' and indicating 'Informal comments on earlier search results'). Such informal comments will be transmitted to the ISA and IB and will be published on PATENTSCOPE. Check Annex D for which ISAs offer this service (paragraph 7.002A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and basis of the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the international search is to discover relevant prior art — everything made available to the public by written disclosure — that can help determine novelty, inventive step (obviousness), and prior public availability before the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The international search is made on the basis of the claims, with due regard to the description and drawings. Results are set out in the international search report (Article 15(4), Rule 33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of documents to be searched (minimum documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA must endeavor to discover as much relevant prior art as facilities permit and must in any case consult the 'minimum documentation' (list of major patent collections, published PCT applications, and certain technical periodicals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an ISA has more than the minimum documentation available it is obliged to consult that additional documentation to the extent permitted by its facilities (Article 15(4), Rule 34.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of later‑submitted missing parts for the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search will usually be carried out on the basis of the application containing the later submitted missing parts or corrected elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inclusion/incorporation by reference of missing parts is notified to the ISA only after it has begun to draw up the search report, the ISA may invite the applicant to pay an additional fee within one month to consider them. If not paid, the ISA will prepare the search report and written opinion without taking into account the missing parts (Rule 20.5, Rule 20.5bis, Rule 40bis.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirements for international search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application discloses nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences required to be included in a sequence listing and a listing complying with the prescribed standard in a language accepted by the ISA has not been furnished, the ISA may invite the applicant to furnish such a listing or translation and, if applicable, to pay a late furnishing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listing is required for the purpose of carrying out the international search; national law concerning disclosure of sequence listings is for the national phase. The ISA may require the standard‑compliant listing (Rule 5.2, Rule 13ter.1, Section 208, Section 513(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended software for sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO Sequence is recommended for preparation of sequence listings in electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use WIPO Sequence to ensure compliance with the prescribed electronic sequence listing standard (paragraph 7.008).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirements for electronic carriers containing sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: A diskette or other electronic carrier acceptable to the competent ISA must have a permanent label with: applicant name, title of the invention, a reference number, date data were recorded, computer operating system and name of the competent Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted after the filing date, labels must also include the filing date and the application number (Annex F - Appendix IV - 2.(f) of the Administrative Instructions).
